node.title: Re^3: How to declare a dependency on PerlIO in a CPAN module?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Fortunately, most of the code does not rely on being able to use in-memory filehandles, only the feature for parsing "application/warc-fields" from a string. Unfortunately, that feature is how the test suite tests parsing

Here's something that works down to at least 5.6, or just use [doc://File::Temp] in the first place, or [mod://IO::String] for that matter:

sub tempfh { my $data = shift; my $fh; eval { open $fh, "<", \$data or die $!; 1 } or do { require File::Temp; $fh = File::Temp::tempfile(); print $fh $data; seek $fh, 0, 0 or die "seek: $!"; }; return $fh; }

However, having worked quite heavily with tied filehandles myself, I can say: They're neat, and allow for some cool stuff like my [mod://File::Replace::Inplace] module, but I strongly recommend against making them a central part of your API unless you have to. There's various issues across various version of Perl - for example, look at the hoops I have to jump through in [https://metacpan.org/source/HAUKEX/File-Replace-0.14/t/25_tie_handle_argv.t#L41|t/25_tie_handle_argv.t lines 41-49 (and 70-71)] just to get the tests working. And even in my module [mod://File::Replace], I've come to prefer the API without tied filehandles, even though I initially [id://1199805|thought] they were pretty neat.

So from my experience let me suggest: use tied filehandles if they're the only way to provide certain APIs (such as my [mod://File::Replace::Inplace], or the transparent uncompression of the IO::Uncompress::* family), but otherwise, make your API OO based (modeling it on [doc://IO::Handle], if you like), and provide a tied API only as an optional layer of sugar.

Update: Improved wording.
